title: Spooder registry entry
description: One installable thing: a module (a backend half, a WebUI half, or both) or a plugin.

id.description: Stable identifier. A module: the module name Spooder registers it under, so it must match the backend manifest's spooder_module.name. A plugin: 'owner/name', like an npm scope - owner is the GitHub account that publishes it (must match plugin.repo's owner) and name is the plugin's own name, the folder it installs under. The owner part is what keeps two authors' 'chatbox' from colliding.

legacyNames.description: Plugins only. Folder names this plugin was installed under before it had this id, e.g. from a hand-installed zip. An installed plugin with one of these names is treated as this entry: it shows as installed and updates in place, keeping its folder, settings and overlay layers.

summary.description: One line, shown on the card. Say what it does, not that it is a Spooder module.

spooder.description: Which Spooder versions this runs on, as a semver range. Entries outside the host's version are shown but not installable.

track.description: pinned - install exactly the version below, whose sha256 a reviewer checked. latest - follow the repo's newest release, which trades that check for not needing a registry PR per release.

asset.description: Release asset filename. Omitted for a 'latest' entry, which takes the release's first asset.
